RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the July 24, 2006/Sravana 2, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Development of North Eastern Region; Food Processing Industries;
Human Resource Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs;
Non-Conventional Energy Sources; Ocean Development; Power; Science and
Technology; Social Justice and Empowerment; Tribal Affairs; Women and
Child Development)
Total number of questions — 20
Royalty on minerals
†*1. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS: Will
the Minister of MINES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government of
Chhattisgarh have requested that royalty
on minerals be fixed on the basis of
percentage of its market value;
(b) whether Planning Commission have
also opined on the same lines;
(c) if so, the reasons for non-
implementation of the same; and
(d) the reasons for non-representation
of the producer-States in the Committee
constituted for this purpose?
Gap between consumption and
generation of power
*2. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL
APTE:
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) the per capita gap between the
consumption and generation of power from
various sources in the country recorded
during the last three years, State-wise;
(b) the total quantum of power supplied
from Central pool to each State during the
period;
(c) whether the gap between
consumption and generation is likely to be
bridged during the ensuing five years;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) the annual percentage of increase
being registered in power generation;
(f) whether it is a fact that the allocation
of funds for the current financial year has
been curtailed; and
(g) if so, the details thereof alongwith
the reasons therefor?
Strategy to balance demand and
supply of power
†*3. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
 (a) whether Government have drawn
up any strategy for striking a balance
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

2
between the demand and  supply of power
in the country;
(b) whether Government have
formulated any concrete plan to end distress
being caused by the power crisis in the
national capital of the country; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Vacant posts and pending cases in
courts
*4. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Supreme Court has
directed all the State Governments and UTs
to draw out a schedule for timely filling up
of vacancies of judges to clear pending
litigations;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what was the volume of pendency
of cases in the High Courts in 2005 and
how far it has increased since 2004?
Electrification of villages
*5. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have launched
'Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran
Yojana' with an aim to provide electricity
to every home within five years;
(b) if so, the details thereof, particularly
in Andhra Pradesh;
(c) whether Government have drawn
any scheme to tap the available sources
of alternative energy to meet the set
targets;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) the number of villages likely to be
covered for electrification in each State
during 2006-07;
(f) the allocation made for the same;
(g) the steps Government propose to
take to achieve the aim; and
(h) the role of NTPC, NHPC and Power
Grid Corporation under this programme?
Bio-mass energy for villages
*6. KUMARI NIRMALA DESH-
PANDE: Will the Minister of NON-
CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal to
launch a mission for using bio-mass energy
for villages in a big way;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Groups to assist Oversight
Committee
*7. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of groups that have been
set up to assist Oversight Committee
which has been entrusted the work of
preparing a roadmap for implementation
of 27 per cent quota for OBCs in all
educational institutions;
(b) whether it is a fact that Government
have assured the Oversight Committee that
it would provide Rs. 4,000 crores for
expansion of infrastructure in educational
institutions where the reservation policy
is going to be implemented; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?

3
World Bank's report on election
expenditure
†*8. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the World
Bank has recently published a report
regarding expenses incurred by the
candidates in elections in the country;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that in
this report, the elections in India have been
termed as comparatively more expensive;
and
(c) if so, Government's reaction thereto
and the future proposals to check election
expenses?
Mineral reserves in the country

SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH

Total number of questions — 75
Setting-up of Food Processing Units
in rural and urban areas
1. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN: Will
the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the details of subsidies/grants
available for setting-up food processing
units in rural/urban areas, separately;
(b) whether it is a fact that subsidies/
grants in respect of certain industries have
been withdrawn recently;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Policy for betterment of FPIs and
Agri-business
2. SHRI T.S.BAJWA: Will the Minister
of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Empowered
Committee of Ministers had approved the
policy for the betterment of food processing
industries and Agri-business;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the areas in which the intending
entrepreneurs are likely to be benefited?
Setting-up of food parks in Uttaranchal
†3. SHRI  HARISH RAWAT: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government of Uttaranchal
has submitted any proposal to his Ministry
with regard to setting-up of food parks;
(b) if so,  the details thereof;
(c) whether his Ministry is considering
any proposal to increase the amount of
Central subsidy to be provided for
construction of food parks; and
(d) if so, the amount proposed to be
fixed for the same?
Central status to Utkal University
4. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
SHRI B. J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

2
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(a) whether it is proposed to grant
Central status to the Utkal University in
Orissa;
(b) if so, the status of the proposal; and
(c) the time-frame within which this
would be done to meet the aspirations of
the people of Orissa?
Establishment of schools for equal
opportunity
†5. SHRI  RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the attention of
Government has been drawn to the
statement of Deputy Chairman of National
Knowledge Commission in which it has
been stated that in the next  10-15 years,
if four lakh additional schools are started,
everybody can get an opportunity;
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that a scheme
has been formulated to implement this
proposal; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Non-essentiality  of NET for
lecturership
†6. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
University Grants Commission has decided
to do away with the essentiality of the
compulsory National Eligibility Test
(NET) for filling up the vacant posts of
Lecturers in the Universities;
(b) whether a delegation of academicians
met the Prime Minister and the Human
Resource Development Minister in this
matter;
(c) if so,  whether any positive steps
have been taken by Government after this
meeting; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Differential fee structure
7. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to introduce a differential fee structure to
suit the paying capacity of every student;
(b) whether Government has received
any recommendations in this regard;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) whether it is a fact that it would not
be prudent to charge the same fee from all
students irrespective of their socio-
economic status?
Higher education as pro-rich and
urban phenomenon
8. SHRIMATI  S.G. INDIRA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that according to
a report it has been found that higher
education is a pro-rich and urban
phenomenon;
(b) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to remove this disparity; and
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
enrolment of the SCs in higher education

3
increased  from 8.6 per cent in  1990-91 to
11.3 per cent in 2002-03 while that of the
STs was from 2.1 per cent to 3.6 per cent?
Unrecognized technical and
professional courses
9. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that many
institutions all over India are offering degree
in technical and professional courses which
are not recognised by Government but have
credential in private sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof
